details: @xokodon430/jsclamp copies the code and README of the npm package clamp and adds a preinstall script (`node setup.js`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. In 1.0.2, setup.js downloads a second stage from https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J, falling back to https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw; the function that would write the download to a random file in the temporary directory and run it is empty, so the stage is fetched but not executed. In 1.0.3 the URL list is empty and the script exits without network activity. setup.js in 1.0.2 is byte-identical to that of clampony 1.0.9 (MAL-2026-20433), and both packages use the same second-stage URLs; that record describes the second stage as a credential stealer that collects Telegram Desktop sessions, SSH keys and cloud and package-registry credentials and sends them to a Telegram bot. The package was published from a newly created account on 2026-11-24. Remediation: remove the package, block the URLs above, and if it was installed, treat credentials on that machine as exposed and rotate them.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
